Hi Asha — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single action list for the private/VPC performance gating work. I kept this focused on the networking and streaming SLOs we discussed.

Summary of ask from Acme:
- Support streaming inference from a private deployment behind your VPC peering/VPN.
- Target production SLOs: 95th-percentile token latency and end-to-end completion latency for interactive flows.
- Target concurrency: sustained concurrent streaming sessions during peak (you mentioned 300–500).

Redwood proposed acceptance gates (initial):
- End-to-end response (complete generation) p95 < 500 ms for 32-token short responses, p95 token latency < 200 ms for streaming windows.
- Sustained concurrency: validate 400 concurrent streaming sessions at median payload (avg 12 tokens/sec/session) without >5% error increase.
- Egress/peering: no sustained packet loss >0.2% and average RTT <30 ms to our inference subnet for 95% of requests.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Acme to provide network contact and current peering/VPN topology (diagram + egress NAT IPs). Attachment: I placed a template diagram to annotate.
2) Redwood to provide a preflight checklist and measurement plan (see attached checklist).
3) Schedule two validation windows: a lightweight connectivity probe (30–60m) and a full concurrency load test (2–4 hrs).
4) Define failure gates for the load test (packet loss, tail latency bands, streams dropped).

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Will streaming go over an IPsec VPN or cloud peering? (This affects MTU and MSS tuning.)
- Are there any middleboxes (WAF, NAT gateway) that re-write ports or terminate TLS?
- Do you require traffic to originate from specific customer subnets / egress IP ranges?

I attached a simple network diagram template (acme_network_diagram_v2.pdf) and our preflight checklist (redwood_private_preflight_checklist.xlsx).

If that looks right, Marissa can propose a pair of windows next week; Ben will own the load test plan and tuning recommendations.

Thanks — Hannah

Thanks — adding concrete recommendations from the SRE/Perf side to help the network team triage quickly.

Quick rules-of-thumb for IPsec + streaming (what we will validate in the preflight):
- MTU/MSS: For IPsec tunnels we recommend lowering TCP MSS to ~1350–1400 to avoid fragmentation on encapsulated packets (this aligns with common cloud VPN overhead).
- Keepalive and idle timeouts: configure VPN keepalives < 60s to avoid mid-flight tunnel resets during streaming.
- Port/policy: outbound HTTPS (443) is ideal; if you must pin egress IPs we can accept a small set of prefix ranges — we need at least 2 static egress IPs for active/standby.
- TLS termination: end-to-end TLS preferred (no WAF termination) for best tail latency; if WAF must terminate TLS, ensure it supports HTTP/2 passthrough or preserves chunk boundaries for streaming.

Perf acceptance targets (for the validation run):
- Connectivity probe: RTT median < 20 ms; packet loss < 0.1% across 95% of probes.
- Streaming smoke test (30m): p95 token latency < 200 ms; 99th token latency < 450 ms for short flows (<64 tokens).
- Full concurrency load (2–4 hrs): sustain 400 concurrent streaming sessions with success rate > 98% (<=2% stream errors/drops).
- Resource fallback: if p99 end-to-end >750 ms or error rate >5% during the test, we mark the run as failed and investigate path/codec issues.

Measurement plan highlights:
- We'll run agents from within your VPC/peered path (not the public Internet) and collect packet-level metrics, TCP retran counts, and application-level stream drop counts.
- We will also instrument per-token emit timestamps so we can plot token-latency distribution across sessions.

Known gotchas we've seen:
- PMTU discovery failures on IPsec tunnels causing 1500->fragmentation; lowering MSS fixes majority of issues.
- WAF/TLS termination blocking HTTP/2 chunked responses and converting to buffer mode (this kills streaming).

I'll attach the Redwood preflight checklist and a short table of the port/payload profile we plan to use. Can the Acme network team confirm whether TLS is terminated at the WAF? That will change the mitigation steps.

Cheers,

Proposed fail gates for the probe (quick check):

- Median RTT > 35 ms or RTT p95 > 80 ms

Proposed fail gates for the concurrency run:
- Sustained stream error rate >3% or sudden spike >5%
- p99 end-to-end >750 ms for short flows
